description:
## Goal

Make the command surface tell the truth: root compilation is always closed as one program, and no flag pretends to select behavior that does not exist.

## Current proof

Both source and build parsers accept --lto and --whole-program with empty match arms. The help text calls them compatibility flags, while guides/modules.html claims they enable a distinct optimizer mode and advises users when to select it. There is no mode bit or downstream consumer.

## Strategy

Add red CLI parser and process tests requiring both spellings to fail as unknown arguments. Delete both parser arms and every usage/help mention. Rewrite the modules guide around unconditional root closure and remove the LTO section and navigation entry rather than preserving historical language.

## Signal

Repository search finds no CLI option or guide instruction for lto or whole-program. Ordinary run and build behavior is unchanged. Focused CLI tests, guide checks, full library and CLI suites, formatting, workspace checks, and strict clippy pass.

## Deletion

Remove the two empty parser branches, help and usage vocabulary, obsolete guide section, examples, and compatibility assertions. Add no alias, hidden option, warning path, or tombstone comment.
title: Delete no-op LTO compatibility modes and document unconditional root closure
